content.thinking:
I'm checking each claim against its sources. The root cause is attributed to F1, which says it's unverified, and it's backed by F1 and G5309. The plain-words version says an admin turned on a monthly-spending feature on the shop's account page, and I'm noting that "new" isn't stated in the record, a minor point. It also says the feature then failed with a division by zero, likely for shoppers with no purchases this month, which is hedged and rests on F1 and G5309.

Next I'm checking the still-at-risk claim, which rests on hedged wording and the fix that remains in place, and the symptom claim about account pages failing for many shoppers, supported by the error rate. The causal chain's timing holds up against the logs, though one line blurs the ClientDisconnected failures that came before the onset.

I'm working through the remaining checks on the contributing factors: there's no record of a review step before the switch, and the flag went from off to on for all account page traffic at once, with no staged rollout visible.

I'm checking the went-wrong claim about the alert not being linked to an on-call incident against the record, which says the same thing in slightly different words, so it holds. The "every request failed" line isn't in the document, so I'm leaving it out.

supported.quote: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page works out its spend figure in `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month`. For a shopper who has bought nothing this month that number is zero, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and the request fails. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

An administrator switched on a new monthly-spending feature on the shop's account page, and the code it turned on then failed with a division by zero, likely for shoppers who had bought nothing this month.
Account pages could fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month if monthly-spend-feature is switched back on.
Account pages failed for many shoppers
rows: The same rate while it was broken: 26.8%

supported.quote: Shoppers' account page requests failed: the service logged a rise in account page errors and failed account page requests.
The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. These errors were first logged in the onset minute and kept appearing until the logs read end.

The code path that raised the error was turned on when admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at {P1.1}. In the service's own flag evaluations, every evaluation read off before the switch, the evaluations were split between off and on in the minute of the switch, and every evaluation read on after it.
A deployment: no deploy came back for the {T8.2} day {T8.3} minute before {T8.4}. All {T12.2} replicas ran a single revision, and the metrics read show the service healthy before the onset.
rows: The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 1.0%

supported.quote: Any other flag change: the flag provider's history showed {T15.2} flag change by anyone but Argus in the {T15.3} hour before {T15.4}, and that change is this switch-on.

With the flag on, the account page's spend figure goes through a function that divides by the number of purchases the shopper made this month. That number is zero for a shopper who has bought nothing this month, so the division fails.
No check was seen that ran the code path behind monthly-spend-feature for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on in production.
The flag went from off to on for all account page traffic at once: evaluations were split only during the minute of the switch and were all on from the next minute. No staged rollout was seen.
No on-call person was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.
